voiceover: You build a login form, someone types a quote mark into the username box, and your app crashes with a database error. That error means your data is at risk. Here's why. If your code glues user input straight into a SQL query, the database can't tell your code apart from their text. A quote can end your string early, and whatever comes after gets run as part of the query. That's SQL injection. The fix is simple: parameterized queries. You send the query with a placeholder, and the input separately. The database treats the input as plain data, never as code. Most database libraries support this. Part two: when the input is HTML.
